Valid for: 2026/27

Main field:  Communication Systems
      
      
        Depth of study relative to the degree requirements:  Second cycle, in-depth level of the course cannot be classified
      
      
Elective for: D4-hs, D4-is, E4-ns, E5-hp, F4, MMSR2, MSOC1, MWIR1, Pi4
Language of instruction: The course will be given in English

The course aims to provide students with a comprehensive, hands-on understanding of hardware-level security. It will focus on the theory and practice of power side-channel analysis, fault injection (glitching), and microarchitectural attacks. Students will use tools like the ChipWhisperer platform, the Mastik software, and machine learning techniques to gain the practical skills necessary to identify, execute, and mitigate these advanced threats in modern computer/embedded systems.

Basics of Hardware Hacking: The shift from software to hardware-level security. Understanding physical attack surfaces on embedded systems and SoCs.
Power Side-Channel Attacks with ChipWhisperer: Understanding how power consumption relates to data processing, how this opens up for attacks and how to counter this.
Fault Injection Attacks with ChipWhisperer: Intentionally introducing errors into a system to disrupt its normal operation, and how to counter this.
Microarchitectural Attacks: Modern CPU & Memory Architecture: In-depth look at CPU caches, memory hierarchy, DRAM, and speculative execution work as attack surfaces, and mitigation techniques.

Grading scale: TH - (U, 3, 4, 5) - (Fail, Three, Four, Five)
Assessment:

Assessment is based on three mandatory laboratory assignments and a final report. All labs must receive a passing grade to be eligible to submit the report. The final grade (3, 4, 5) is determined by the quality of the report and an accompanying oral presentation.

The examiner, in consultation with Disability Support Services, may deviate from the regular form of examination in order to provide a permanently disabled student with a form of examination equivalent to that of a student without a disability.

Code: 0126. Name: Laboratory Work. 

Credits: 4.5. Grading scale: UG - (U, G).
        
          Assessment: Active participation in laboratory work.
        
        
          The module includes: Three Labs.
        
        
          Further information: A passing grade (G) on this module is required to be eligible to submit the final project.
        
        
Code: 0226. Name: Project. 

Credits: 3.0. Grading scale: TH - (U, 3, 4, 5).
        
          Assessment: A project graded on the scale of U, 3, 4, or 5

        
        
          The module includes: A written project report and an accompanying oral presentation.
        
        
          Further information: This module's grade determines the final grade for the entire course.
